docs.title: floci-oci
docs.text:
Light, fluffy, and always free — now for Oracle Cloud

floci-oci is a fast, free, and open-source local Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) emulator built for developers who need reliable OCI services in development and CI without cost, complexity, or vendor lock-in.

It implements real OCI wire protocols so the official OCI SDKs, the OCI CLI, Terraform, and OpenTofu work unchanged against http://localhost:4599.

docs.title: The Floci family
docs.text: Emulator Cloud Port floci AWS 4566 floci-az Azure 4577 floci-gcp GCP 4588 floci-oci OCI 4599

docs.title: Supported services
docs.text: Service API Coverage Identity (IAM) /20160918/… Compartments, users, groups, memberships, policies, availability and fault domains, regions, region subscriptions, tenancy, work requests Object Storage /n/{ns}/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Namespaces, buckets, objects, listing, rename, copy, multipart uploads, pre-authenticated requests, work requests Queue /20210201/… Queues, messages, visibility timeouts, dead-letter queues, stats Vault, KMS & Secrets /20180608/…, /20190301/… Vaults, keys, real AES-GCM/RSA/ECDSA crypto, secrets and bundles Streaming /20180418/… Streams, partitions, cursors, consumer groups Functions /20181201/… Applications, functions, real invocation via an Fn Project sidecar Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) /20180222/… Clusters, node pools, options, kubeconfig generation, work requests, real k3s sidecar Database with PostgreSQL /20220915/… DB systems, start/stop/restart, password reset, connection details, shapes, default configurations, work requests, real PostgreSQL sidecar Organizations /20230401/… Child tenancies, organizations, organization tenancies, links, work requests

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
docker compose up -d
curl http://localhost:4599/_floci-oci/health
oci os ns get --endpoint http://localhost:4599

See the Quick Start for details.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome! floci-oci follows the same architecture and conventions as its siblings floci (AWS), floci-az and floci-gcp.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Requirements: JDK 25, Docker (for the compat suite).

./mvnw quarkus:dev     # dev mode on port 4599
./mvnw test            # unit + integration tests
make test-java-compat  # oci-java-sdk suite against a running emulator

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
io.floci.oci
├── config/           EmulatorConfig (@ConfigMapping prefix floci-oci)
├── core/
│   ├── common/       OciException/mapper, opc-request-id filter, Ocids, OciPage, Etags,
│   │                 ServiceRegistry + self-registering ServiceDescriptor
│   ├── auth/         OCI Signature parsing (never verified)
│   ├── storage/      StorageBackend (memory/persistent/hybrid/wal), tenancy isolation
│   └── workrequest/  Shared async-operation plane
├── lifecycle/        Boot/shutdown, init hooks, /health + /_floci-oci/*
└── services/<svc>/   Controller (JAX-RS) → Service → model/Stored*.java

docs.title: Adding a new OCI service
docs.text:
1. Create services/<svc>/ with <Svc>Controller, <Svc>Service, model/
  2. The service registers its own ServiceDescriptor in an @Observes StartupEvent method, adding a service must never require a service-keyed switch in core
  3. Add <Svc>ServiceConfig { enabled(); } to EmulatorConfig.ServicesConfig + the YAML block
  4. Wire storage through StorageFactory
  5. Add the test trio: <Svc>ServiceTest (unit), <Svc>RestIntegrationTest, <Svc>DisabledRestIntegrationTest (asserts 503)
  6. Validate against the real SDK in compatibility-tests/
  7. Add docs/services/<svc>.md and the mkdocs nav entry

Never invent protocol behavior. Check the wire contract against the OCI SDK sources (the oci-go-sdk generated models are the closest thing OCI has to a machine-readable wire model).

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
AGENTS.md carries the full list. The rules worth knowing before your first PR:

  • Write explicit types. Do not use var. The concrete type at a call site is usually what a wire-contract reviewer needs to see. The one exception is a record deconstruction pattern.
  • Import the classes you use. No fully-qualified names inline, except for a genuine name collision in that file, with a comment saying what collides.
  • No wildcard imports in src/main. Static wildcards are fine in tests.
  • Never leave a catch block empty. If swallowing is correct, name the variable ignored or expected and say why in a comment.
  • Always use braces in conditionals, and use constructor injection.
  • Tests: JUnit 5 with Hamcrest and RestAssured. Name methods as a camelCase sentence or method_scenario_expectation, never testX.
  • Docs: no em-dashes. Use colons, commas, or periods.

Existing code does not yet satisfy all of these everywhere. Match the rules in code you add or change; leave unrelated cleanups for their own PR.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Conventional commits: feat:, fix:, perf:, docs:, chore:
  • Keep changes focused; behaviour changes come with a test
  • See AGENTS.md for the full operating rules

Please keep no more than 4 open pull requests, drafts included, and no more than 2 of them ready for review. A bot turns a 3rd ready PR back into a draft and closes new ones opened while you already have 4 open. See CONTRIBUTING.md for details.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Stable releases ship on the 15th and the last day of each month. Merging to main does not cut a release: the change rides the next train, and reaches the nightly image on the next nightly build.

Releases are cut from main by the Release Cut workflow, scheduled at 00:30 US Central time on those days (maintainers can also run it by hand). It runs semantic-release over the Conventional Commits since the last tag. That is why the commit type matters: feat: and fix: move the version, docs: and chore: do not. CHANGELOG.md is generated from those messages and is not edited by hand; a genuine correction goes in a PR carrying the changelog-edit label.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
All configuration lives under the floci-oci.* prefix; every property maps to an FLOCI_OCI_* environment variable via the standard MicroProfile Config rules (dots and dashes become underscores, uppercase).

Variable Default Description FLOCI_OCI_PORT 4599 Listen port FLOCI_OCI_BASE_URL http://localhost:4599 Base URL used in returned URLs FLOCI_OCI_HOSTNAME – Overrides the hostname in returned URLs (multi-container setups) FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_REGION us-ashburn-1 Home region given to a tenancy the first time it is seen, which is also where its requests land when the Host names no OCI region FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_REALM oc1 Realm key for OCIDs when the region is not a known OCI region; known regions use their own realm (e.g. uk-gov-london-1 is oc4) FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_TENANCY_ID ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocal… Tenancy used for unsigned requests FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_NAMESPACE floci-local Object Storage namespace FLOCI_OCI_MAX_REQUEST_SIZE 2048 Max request body size in MB FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_MODE memory memory, persistent, hybrid, or wal FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_PERSISTENT_PATH ./data Where persisted state is written FLOCI_OCI_AUTH_REQUIRE_SIGNATURE false Reject unsigned requests with 401. /health, /_floci-oci/* and pre-authenticated requests (/p/*) are always exempt FLOCI_OCI_TLS_ENABLED false Serve HTTPS + HTTP on the same port FLOCI_OCI_TLS_HTTPS_PORT 443 Extra HTTPS binding for clients that assume 443 (0 disables) FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_IDENTITY_ENABLED true Enable/disable Identity FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OBJECTSTORAGE_ENABLED true Enable/disable Object Storage FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_QUEUE_ENABLED true Enable/disable Queue FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_KMS_ENABLED true Enable/disable KMS (vaults, keys, crypto) FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_VAULT_ENABLED true Enable/disable Vault secrets + bundles FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_STREAMING_ENABLED true Enable/disable Streaming FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_ORGANIZATIONS_ENABLED true Enable/disable Organizations (child tenancies, organizations, links) FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_FUNCTIONS_ENABLED true Enable/disable Functions FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_FUNCTIONS_MOCK false Skip the Fn sidecar; invocations return a synthetic body FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_FUNCTIONS_SERVER_IMAGE fnproject/fnserver:latest Fn Project server image FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_ENABLED true Enable/disable Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_MOCK false Skip the k3s sidecar; clusters become ACTIVE at once with synthetic endpoints FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_DEFAULT_IMAGE rancher/k3s:v1.30.1-k3s1 k3s image for cluster sidecars FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_API_SERVER_BASE_PORT 6443 First host port for cluster API servers FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_API_SERVER_MAX_PORT 6543 Last host port for cluster API servers FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_KUBECONFIG_AUTH exec Kubeconfig user: exec (real OKE oci ce cluster generate-token) or token (static bearer token) FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 300 How long a cluster may stay CREATING before it goes FAILED FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_ENABLED true Enable/disable Database with PostgreSQL FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_MOCK false Skip the PostgreSQL sidecar; DB systems become ACTIVE at once with nothing listening on their endpoint FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_IMAGE postgres:{major}-alpine PostgreSQL image for DB system sidecars; {major} is replaced with the major of the DB system's dbVersion FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_BASE_PORT 15432 First host port for DB system endpoints FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_MAX_PORT 15531 Last host port for DB system endpoints FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 120 How long a DB system may take to accept connections before it goes FAILED FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_DOCKER_NETWORK – Shared Docker network for sidecar containers FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_RESOURCE_NAMESPACE – Namespace inserted into sidecar container/volume names (floci-oci-<ns>-…) so parallel emulator instances on one Docker host don't collide FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_ENDPOINT_MODE auto How a sidecar's published port is addressed in the endpoints returned to clients: auto (localhost when floci-oci runs on the host, the sidecar's container name when it runs in a container) or published (always the Docker daemon's host and the published port; for a remote daemon, or host-side clients of a containerised floci-oci). Only services that build their client endpoint from this setting follow it: OKE cluster endpoints do not, and are always 127.0.0.1

Per-service storage overrides use the map form:

FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_SERVICES_OBJECTSTORAGE_MODE=wal
FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_SERVICES_OBJECTSTORAGE_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS=5000

docs.title: Resource identity labels
docs.text:
Every container and volume floci-oci creates carries the base labels floci=true, floci_emulator=floci-oci and, when FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_RESOURCE_NAMESPACE is set, floci_namespace. Function containers that fnserver starts itself are not labelled. A container backing an emulated OCI resource also carries labels tying it back to that resource, additive to the base labels:

Label Value Purpose io.floci oci Cloud provider, for multi-cloud discovery when several Floci emulators share a host io.floci.service e.g. oke The OCI service the container backs io.floci.resource-id e.g. ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.… The resource OCID, as the OCI CLI and SDKs take it io.floci.compartment the compartment OCID The compartment the resource belongs to io.floci.region e.g. us-ashburn-1 The region the resource belongs to (an OKE cluster's own region). The shared Fn server serves every region and carries no region label floci_service same value as io.floci.service Legacy alias, written alongside io.floci.service; prefer the new key

This makes docker ps --filter label=io.floci.resource-id=<cluster-ocid> resolve an emulated resource to its backing container directly. Applied to Container Engine (OKE) clusters and Functions. The Functions fnserver container is a shared singleton serving every application, so it carries every label except io.floci.resource-id and io.floci.compartment.

The io.floci.* key set is shared with floci-aws, floci-gcp and floci-az, so docker ps --filter label=io.floci lists every resource-backing container on a shared host.

docs.title: Initialization Hooks
docs.text:
floci-oci runs shell scripts from lifecycle-phase directories, mirroring the other Floci emulators.

Phase Directory When boot /etc/floci-oci/init/boot.d Before services initialize — OCI APIs are not available yet start /etc/floci-oci/init/start.d After the HTTP server is listening ready /etc/floci-oci/init/ready.d After start hooks complete shutdown /etc/floci-oci/init/stop.d (or shutdown.d) On graceful shutdown

Scripts run in lexicographic order. A failing start/ready script aborts startup.

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  floci-oci:
    volumes:
      - ./init-scripts:/etc/floci-oci/init/ready.d

#!/bin/sh
# init-scripts/10-create-bucket.sh
oci os bucket create --endpoint http://localhost:4599 \
  --compartment-id "$FLOCI_OCI_DEFAULT_TENANCY_ID" \
  --namespace floci-local --name seeded-bucket

Hook state is inspectable at GET /_floci-oci/init.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Property Default Description floci-oci.init-hooks.shell-executable /bin/sh Interpreter for hook scripts floci-oci.init-hooks.timeout-seconds 30 Per-script timeout floci-oci.init-hooks.shutdown-grace-period-seconds 2 Grace period for shutdown hooks

docs.title: Storage Modes
docs.text:
floci-oci supports four storage modes, selected globally with floci-oci.storage.mode (FLOCI_OCI_STORAGE_MODE) and overridable per service.

Mode Behaviour Use case memory (default) Everything in memory, lost on restart Fast tests, CI persistent Write-through JSON files on every change Durability over speed hybrid In-memory with periodic flush to disk Balanced local development wal Write-ahead log + periodic snapshot compaction Durability with fast writes

Persistent state is written under floci-oci.storage.persistent-path (default ./data, /app/data in the Docker image — mount a volume to keep it).

docs.title: Per-service overrides
docs.text:
floci-oci:
  storage:
    mode: memory
    services:
      objectstorage:
        mode: wal
        flush-interval-ms: 5000

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text: Every storage key is transparently prefixed with the calling tenancy's OCID, so requests signed with different tenancy OCIDs see fully isolated resources.

docs.title: OCI CLI & SDK Setup
docs.text: floci-oci parses the OCI request signature for tenancy/user context but never verifies the RSA signature — any locally generated API key works. No account, no real credentials.

docs.title: OCI CLI
docs.text:
Create a throwaway key and config once:

mkdir -p ~/.oci
openssl genrsa -out ~/.oci/floci_key.pem 2048

cat > ~/.oci/config <<'EOF'
[FLOCI]
user=ocid1.user.oc1..flocilocaluser0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000
fingerprint=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99
tenancy=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
region=us-ashburn-1
key_file=~/.oci/floci_key.pem
EOF

Then point the CLI at the emulator:

oci --profile FLOCI os ns get --endpoint http://localhost:4599

docs.title: Java SDK
docs.text:
KeyPair pair = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").generateKeyPair();
var auth = SimpleAuthenticationDetailsProvider.builder()
        .tenantId("ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000")
        .userId("ocid1.user.oc1..anyuser")
        .fingerprint("aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99")
        .privateKeySupplier(() -> new ByteArrayInputStream(pemOf(pair)))
        .region(Region.US_ASHBURN_1)
        .build();

ObjectStorageClient client = ObjectStorageClient.builder().build(auth);
client.setEndpoint("http://localhost:4599");

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
import oci

config = {
    "user": "ocid1.user.oc1..anyuser",
    "fingerprint": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:11:22:33:44:55:66:77:88:99",
    "tenancy": "ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    "region": "us-ashburn-1",
    "key_file": "~/.oci/floci_key.pem",
}
client = oci.object_storage.ObjectStorageClient(
    config, service_endpoint="http://localhost:4599")
print(client.get_namespace().data)

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text: The tenancy OCID in your signing key's keyId is the storage partition — requests signed with different tenancy OCIDs see isolated resources. Unsigned requests fall back to the configured floci-oci.default-tenancy-id.

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
Regional resources (buckets, queues, streams, vaults, keys, secrets, functions, clusters) are partitioned by region as well as tenancy. The region comes from the request Host header: the first dot-separated label that is a known OCI region name, so any host that names a region works in it. The simplest way to send one is the public wildcard <service>.<region>.localhost.floci.io, which resolves to 127.0.0.1: for example http://messaging.us-phoenix-1.localhost.floci.io:4599 works in us-phoenix-1. Any other host, such as localhost:4599, reaches the tenancy's home region. Regional OCIDs carry the three letter region key (ocid1.queue.oc1.phx.…), as real Object Storage bucket OCIDs do; some newer OCI services use the full region name there instead.

Identity is global, as on real OCI: compartments, users, groups and policies are shared by every region of the tenancy. Each tenancy has its own home region: a tenancy seen for the first time gets default-region, and keeps it if default-region changes later. As on real OCI, Identity writes are only accepted at the home region (403 NotAllowed elsewhere), and a tenancy can only use a region it is subscribed to (401 NotAuthenticated otherwise): the home region always is, and CreateRegionSubscription adds another at once. See Identity for the details.

Data persisted by an older floci-oci, before region partitioning, is moved into default-region on startup.

docs.title: Run the emulator
docs.text:
Docker ComposeMaven (dev mode) 
docker compose up -d

./mvnw quarkus:dev

The emulator listens on port 4599. Verify it is up:

curl http://localhost:4599/_floci-oci/health

docs.title: First requests
docs.text:
# Object Storage namespace
curl http://localhost:4599/n
# → "floci-local"

# Create a bucket
curl -X POST http://localhost:4599/n/floci-local/b \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"demo","compartmentId":"ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"}'

# Upload and fetch an object
curl -X PUT http://localhost:4599/n/floci-local/b/demo/o/hello.txt -d 'hello oci'
curl http://localhost:4599/n/floci-local/b/demo/o/hello.txt

docs.title: With the OCI CLI
docs.text:
oci os ns get --endpoint http://localhost:4599
oci os bucket list --endpoint http://localhost:4599 \
  --compartment-id ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 \
  --namespace floci-local

Or use the bundled wrapper that injects the endpoint automatically:

bin/ocilocal os ns get

Authentication is parsed but never verified — any locally generated API key works. See OCI CLI & SDK Setup.

docs.title: Services Overview
docs.text: Service API root Coverage Identity (IAM) /20160918/… Compartments, users, groups, memberships, policies, reference data, work requests Object Storage /n/{ns}/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Buckets, objects, listing, rename, copy, batch delete, multipart, pre-authenticated requests Queue /20210201/… Queues (work-request driven), messages with visibility timeouts and DLQ, stats, channels Vault, KMS & Secrets /20180608/…, /20190301/… Vaults, keys and versions, real AES-GCM/RSA/ECDSA crypto, secrets and bundles Streaming /20180418/… Streams, partitioned log, cursors (incl. group cursors), commit/heartbeat Functions /20181201/… Applications, functions, real invocation via an fnproject/fnserver sidecar Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) /20180222/… Clusters CRUD, Node Pools CRUD, Options, Kubeconfig generation, work requests, real k3s sidecar Database with PostgreSQL /20220915/… DB systems CRUD, start/stop/restart, password reset, connection details with a CA certificate, shapes, default configurations, work requests, real PostgreSQL sidecar Organizations /20230401/… Child tenancies with their own home region and isolated storage, organizations, organization tenancies, links, work requests

docs.title: Wire contract
docs.text:
Every service follows the OCI wire contract:

  • Errors are {"code": "...", "message": "..."} with the correct HTTP status; missing resources report 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound exactly as real OCI does.
  • Every response carries an opc-request-id header (echoing yours if provided), and opc-client-request-id is echoed back.
  • Lists paginate via limit/page query parameters and the opc-next-page response header. Identity lists return bare JSON arrays.
  • Mutations carry etag headers and honour if-match / if-none-match.
  • Async operations return 202 + opc-work-request-id, pollable via the work-request endpoints.

docs.title: Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE)
docs.text: The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Container Engine for Kubernetes (OKE) emulator service provides local Kubernetes cluster lifecycle management, node pool configuration, kubeconfig generation, and real-mode Kubernetes cluster sidecar execution.

docs.title: Service / API / SDK Client
docs.text: Area API Endpoint SDK Client OKE Clusters /20180222/clusters ContainerEngineClient OKE Node Pools /20180222/nodePools ContainerEngineClient OKE Options /20180222/options ContainerEngineClient OKE Kubeconfig /20180222/clusters/{clusterId}/kubeconfig/content ContainerEngineClient OKE Work Requests /20180222/workRequests ContainerEngineClient

docs.title: Supported Operations
docs.text: Area Operations Clusters CreateCluster, GetCluster, ListClusters, UpdateCluster, DeleteCluster, CreateKubeconfig Node Pools CreateNodePool, GetNodePool, ListNodePools, UpdateNodePool, DeleteNodePool Options GetClusterOptions, GetNodePoolOptions Work Requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs

docs.title: Real-Mode k3s Docker Integration
docs.text:
When real mode is enabled (FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_MOCK=false), OKE provisions real local Kubernetes clusters using rancher/k3s:v1.30.1-k3s1 Docker sidecar containers:

  • Control Plane: Each sidecar runs k3s server (Traefik disabled), a self-contained single-node control plane that needs no external server or join token.
  • Dynamic Port Allocation: Each cluster's Kubernetes API server is bound to a dynamic host port in the configured range (default: 6443..6543). The port is published on all host interfaces, so the API is reachable from other machines that can reach the host.
  • Lifecycle: CreateCluster returns the cluster CREATING with an IN_PROGRESS work request. floci-oci polls the k3s API in the background; once it answers, the cluster becomes ACTIVE and the work request SUCCEEDED, which is what Terraform and oci ce cluster create --wait-for-state wait on. A sidecar that exits, or an API that is not ready within FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 300), marks both FAILED.
  • kubectl Authentication: The kubeconfig is the real OKE token version 2.0.0 shape: its user runs oci ce cluster generate-token --cluster-id <ocid> --region <region>, and its cluster entry carries the k3s CA, so TLS is verified. k3s does not know these tokens, so it sends each one to floci-oci in a Kubernetes TokenReview (a token webhook meant for the k3s sidecar and unauthenticated like every /_floci-oci endpoint, at /_floci-oci/oke/token-webhook/<tenancy>/<cluster>, the same design as floci-aws EKS).
  • What the webhook checks: the token must be the signed https://containerengine.<region>.oraclecloud.com/cluster_request/<cluster-ocid> URL generate-token builds, for this cluster and its region, with an rsa-sha256 Signature over date (request-target) host, a keyId in the cluster's tenancy, and a date within 5 minutes. Like every floci-oci request, the RSA signature itself is not verified, and there is no IAM policy evaluation: a well-formed token for the cluster is accepted as cluster-admin (system:masters). Real OKE verifies the signature and applies IAM policy.
  • Prerequisites for kubectl: the oci CLI on PATH with a config whose key can sign (any key works, since signatures are not verified). Session or security-token auth (--auth security_token) is not supported yet.
  • Static token alternative: Each cluster also gets a random API token, stored with the cluster and never returned by CreateCluster, GetCluster or ListClusters. Set FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_KUBECONFIG_AUTH=token to receive it in the kubeconfig instead of the exec user, for clients without the oci CLI. It is cluster-admin on that cluster.
  • Storage Persistence: Cluster state is stored in a Docker named volume (/var/lib/rancher/k3s) obeying the global storage persistence and prune-volumes-on-delete policies.
  • Mock Mode: Setting FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_OKE_MOCK=true (default in test profiles) bypasses Docker execution and returns synthetic control plane state instantly.
  • Teardown: DELETE and application shutdown remove the sidecar container and keep or drop the named volume by the policy above, so a persistent cluster comes back after a restart. POST /_floci-oci/state/reset forgets every cluster and so always removes its volume too, whatever prune-volumes-on-delete says. The anonymous volumes the k3s image declares always go with the container.

docs.title: Wire & Behavior Notes
docs.text:
• Kubeconfig Generation: POST /20180222/clusters/{id}/kubeconfig/content accepts the SDK's CreateClusterKubeconfigContentDetails (tokenVersion, expiration, endpoint). expiration is deprecated in the SDK and ignored. endpoint must be one of LEGACY_KUBERNETES, PUBLIC_ENDPOINT, PRIVATE_ENDPOINT or VCN_HOSTNAME (any case; otherwise 400 InvalidParameter); floci-oci has one reachable API address, https://127.0.0.1:{hostPort}, so every value resolves to it. Before the cluster is ACTIVE (or in mock mode) there is no CA yet, and the kubeconfig falls back to insecure-skip-tls-verify: true.
  • Work Requests: Asynchronous mutations (such as cluster and node pool creation or deletion) return 202 Accepted with an opc-work-request-id header, pollable via /20180222/workRequests/{id}.
  • Immutable Container Naming: Sidecar containers are named using the immutable cluster OCID (floci-oci-oke-ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.xxx), ensuring display name updates via UpdateCluster do not affect container lifecycle or teardown.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

# Create a cluster
oci ce cluster create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --name demo-cluster --vcn-id "ocid1.vcn.oc1.iad.demovcn" --kubernetes-version "v1.30.1"

# List clusters
oci ce cluster list $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY"

# Download kubeconfig (once the cluster is ACTIVE, so it carries the CA)
oci ce cluster create-kubeconfig $E --cluster-id "ocid1.cluster.oc1.iad.demo" --file ./kubeconfig

# kubectl runs `oci ce cluster generate-token` for each request; real mode only
KUBECONFIG=./kubeconfig kubectl get namespaces

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: OCI Functions — API version 20181201. This is floci-oci's Docker-sidecar reference service: the management plane is emulated in-process, and real invocations run your function image through a shared Fn Project server — the same open-source engine OCI Functions is built on.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Applications Create, Get, List, Update, Delete, ChangeCompartment Functions Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Invocation InvokeFunction (sync, detached, is-dry-run)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• No work requests anywhere — Functions is synchronous with lifecycle-state polling.
  • Lists are bare JSON arrays; ListFunctions requires applicationId.
  • Exact casing matters: memoryInMBs.
  • imageDigest is deterministic per image and changes when the image changes — Terraform's CustomizeDiff depends on this, otherwise plans drift forever.
  • invokeEndpoint is a stable host-only base URL; invocation is raw binary in, binary out — never JSON-wrapped by the emulator.
  • Deleting an application with functions still in it is a 409.

docs.title: Mock mode vs real invocation
docs.text:
floci-oci.services.functions.mock Behaviour false (default) Starts a shared fnproject/fnserver container on first invoke, mirrors the app/function into it, and proxies the call to the real image true No Docker at all; the management plane works fully and invocations return a synthetic body

The test suite sets mock: true so it never needs Docker.

# Disable the sidecar entirely
FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_FUNCTIONS_MOCK=true

Real invocation requires the Docker socket — the emulator's container mounts it, and fnserver spawns your function containers as siblings.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci fn application create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --display-name demo-app --subnet-ids '["ocid1.subnet.oc1.iad.demo"]'
oci fn function create $E --application-id <appId> --display-name hello \
  --image <your-fdk-image>:latest --memory-in-mbs 128
oci fn function invoke $E --function-id <fnId> --body '{"name":"floci"}' --file -

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• Your image must be a current FDK build (http-stream contract). Older fnproject/hello images predate it and fail to initialize.
  • Pre-built functions (PBF listings), provisioned concurrency, trace configs, and detached-invocation result tracking are not implemented.
  • fn-invoke-type: detached returns 202 immediately and runs the function in the background; is-dry-run: true validates without executing.

docs.title: Identity (IAM)
docs.text: OCI Identity and Access Management — API version 20160918.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Resource Operations Compartments Create, Get, List (compartmentIdInSubtree, name, lifecycleState, sortBy, sortOrder, accessLevel), Update, Delete and Move (async, work request), Recover Users Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Groups Create, Get, List, Update, Delete User group memberships AddUserToGroup, Get, List (by user/group), RemoveUserFromGroup Policies Create, Get, List, Update, Delete Availability domains List (3 ADs) Fault domains List (3 per AD) Regions List (every region in the realm of the request's region) Region subscriptions List, Create Tenancies Get Work requests Get, List

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci iam compartment create --endpoint http://localhost:4599 \
  --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --name dev --description "Development"

oci iam compartment list --endpoint http://localhost:4599 --compartment-id "$TENANCY"

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• The root compartment is the tenancy itself; GET /compartments/{tenancyOcid} returns it.
  • Deleting a compartment is asynchronous, like real OCI: 202 + opc-work-request-id. The compartment must be empty, in every region: no child compartments, no policies, and no resources of any other service (buckets, queues, streams, vaults, keys, secrets, functions applications, OKE clusters and node pools). If anything is left, the work request ends FAILED with a Conflict error listing it, and the compartment stays ACTIVE. Otherwise it ends SUCCEEDED and the compartment is DELETED with a random suffix appended to its name (dev.qR5hP2BD), which RecoverCompartment keeps. Deleting a DELETED compartment again succeeds and leaves it unchanged. The work request finishes immediately (real OCI takes a few minutes and passes through DELETING).
  • Compartments nest at most six levels below the tenancy, and a tenancy holds at most 1,000 compartments that are not DELETED, as on real OCI. OCI documents both limits but not their errors, so the codes are emulator choices: creating, moving or recovering a compartment past the depth limit is 400 InvalidParameter, and the count limit is 400 LimitExceeded with a message that starts "Maximum number of compartments", the text the Terraform provider looks for.
  • Availability domains follow the real naming, <prefix>:<region>-AD-<n>: the prefix is Floc for the default tenancy and a stable four letters derived from the OCID for any other, and the region part is PHX and US-ASHBURN for the two original regions and the upper-cased region name elsewhere (Floc:US-ASHBURN-AD-1, Floc:PHX-AD-1, Floc:US-CHICAGO-1-AD-1). Fault domains are FAULT-DOMAIN-1 to FAULT-DOMAIN-3.
  • compartmentIdInSubtree=true is only accepted on the tenancy (root compartment), as on real OCI. accessLevel is validated but not enforced: every compartment is accessible.
  • Region subscriptions complete immediately with status READY. Each tenancy has its own home region, reported by GetTenancy as homeRegionKey: a tenancy seen for the first time gets default-region and keeps it, so changing default-region later does not move an existing tenancy's home.
  • A tenancy can only use the regions it is subscribed to, as on real OCI: a request whose Host names another region returns 401 NotAuthenticated. The home region is always subscribed, and CreateRegionSubscription adds one more at once, so a multi-region setup needs that one call per extra region (by hand or from an init hook). A region outside the tenancy's realm is rejected the same way; OCI documents that rule but not its error code, so the 401 there is an emulator choice. A Host that names no region (localhost) always reaches the tenancy's home region. Emulator endpoints, pre-authenticated requests and CreateRegionSubscription itself are never blocked.
  • Every other service requires its compartmentId to be an ACTIVE compartment created here, or the tenancy itself (the root compartment), as on real OCI: an unknown, deleted or blank one is 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound in a request body and 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound in a query. Create the compartment first, or use the tenancy OCID. The check is skipped only when Identity is disabled, since nothing could then create a compartment.
  • As on real OCI, compartments, users, groups, group memberships and policies can only be created, updated or deleted through the home region's endpoint. A write sent with another region in the Host header returns 403 NotAllowed ("This operation must be directed at the home region."). Reads work in every region, and changes are visible everywhere at once (real OCI takes a few minutes to propagate them). Clients that never set a region host reach their tenancy's home region, so they are unaffected. CreateRegionSubscription is accepted in every region: the SDKs do not tie it to the home region, so floci-oci does not either.
  • Policy statements are stored verbatim; the policy language is not parsed or enforced.
  • Identity domains, API keys, auth tokens, dynamic groups and tag namespaces are not implemented yet.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
Behaviour that OCI's SDKs and documentation do not settle, and what floci-oci does:

  • Compartment names are unique per parent. The SDK's CreateCompartment comment says a name must be unique across the tenancy, while the compartments documentation says two compartments within the same parent can't share a name. floci-oci follows the documentation.
  • MoveCompartment work requests use operation type MOVE_COMPARTMENT. Identity's WorkRequest enum only lists DELETE_COMPARTMENT and DELETE_TAG_DEFINITION.
  • ListRegions lists the regions of the request's realm, the realm of the region named by the Host header (or the home region), since a tenancy can only use regions in its realm.
  • Changes are immediate. Region subscriptions are READY at once (OCI: IN_PROGRESS for several minutes), IAM changes are visible in every region at once (OCI: a few minutes to propagate from the home region), and compartment delete and move work requests finish at once.
  • Error codes OCI does not document for a rule it does document: 400 InvalidParameter for the compartment depth limit, 400 LimitExceeded for the compartment count limit, 401 NotAuthenticated for a region outside the realm, and a Conflict work-request error for a non-empty compartment.

docs.title: Vault, KMS and Secrets
docs.text:
Three OCI services that work together:

Service API SDK client KMS vaults /20180608/vaults KmsVaultClient KMS keys /20180608/keys KmsManagementClient KMS crypto /20180608/{encrypt,decrypt,…} KmsCryptoClient Secrets (management) /20180608/secrets VaultsClient Secrets (retrieval) /20190301/secretbundles SecretsClient

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Vaults Create, Get, List, Update, ScheduleDeletion, CancelDeletion, ChangeCompartment Keys Create, Get, List, Update, Enable, Disable, ScheduleDeletion, CancelDeletion Key versions Create (rotate), Get, List Crypto Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataEncryptionKey, Sign, Verify Secrets CreateSecret, GetSecret, ListSecrets, UpdateSecret, Schedule/CancelDeletion, versions Bundles GetSecretBundle, GetSecretBundleByName, ListSecretBundleVersions

docs.title: Real cryptography
docs.text:
Crypto is not stubbed. Keys hold real material:

  • AES — AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt. The ciphertext envelope carries the key-version id, so ciphertext produced before a rotation still decrypts afterwards.
  • RSA / ECDSA — real JCA sign/verify (SHA_*_RSA_PKCS1_V1_5, ECDSA_SHA_*).
  • plaintextChecksum (CRC32) is returned on Decrypt and GenerateDataEncryptionKey, as the wire contract requires.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• There is no DELETE verb for vaults, keys or secrets — deletion is scheduled via actions/scheduleDeletion and reflected in lifecycleState (PENDING_DELETION), reversible with actions/cancelDeletion.
  • Keys reach ENABLED, not ACTIVE.
  • KeySummary has no keyShape/currentKeyVersion but carries a flat algorithm.
  • The Secret shape never echoes content — content is only readable through a secret bundle.
  • GetSecretBundleByName is a POST with query parameters, no body, and no etag.
  • Single secret versions live at /version/{n} (singular); the list is /versions.

docs.title: Endpoint indirection (deviation)
docs.text:
Real OCI gives each vault its own management/crypto hostname, returned as managementEndpoint / cryptoEndpoint. The OCI SDKs reject endpoints containing a path (endpoint must not contain user info, path, query, or fragment), so the emulator cannot encode the vault in a path suffix and returns its own host for both.

Consequence: CreateKey carries no vaultId, so a new key is attached to the caller's compartment vault — the most recently created ACTIVE one. With the usual one-vault setup this is exact; with several vaults in one compartment, keys land in the newest.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci kms management vault create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --display-name demo-vault --vault-type DEFAULT

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Key import/backup/restore, vault replication, external key managers, secret rotation configs and secret rules are not implemented.

docs.title: Object Storage
docs.text: OCI Object Storage — unversioned paths under /n/{namespace}/b/{bucket}/o/{object}.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Namespace GetNamespace (/n), GetNamespaceMetadata Buckets Create, Get, Head, List, Update, Delete (must be empty) Objects Put (Content-MD5 check, opc-meta-*, conditional headers), Get (Range → 206), Head, Delete Listing ListObjects with prefix/start/end/delimiter/limit/fields, nextStartWith truncation Actions RenameObject; CopyObject (async, work request, terminal status COMPLETED); BatchDeleteObjects (per-object success/failure results, optional per-entry ifMatch, isSkipDeletedResult) Multipart CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, Commit, Abort, List Pre-authenticated requests Create, Get, List, Delete; anonymous data path via /p/{token}/… Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (unversioned at /workRequests)

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"

oci os ns get $E
oci os bucket create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --namespace floci-local --name demo
echo "hello" > /tmp/hello.txt
oci os object put $E --namespace floci-local --bucket-name demo \
  --file /tmp/hello.txt --name hello.txt
oci os object get $E --namespace floci-local --bucket-name demo \
  --name hello.txt --file -

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text:
• Each tenancy has its own namespace, the same in every region, as on real OCI. The default tenancy (unsigned requests, or default-tenancy-id) uses floci-oci.default-namespace (default floci-local); any other signing tenancy gets a stable 12 character namespace derived from its OCID. GetNamespace returns the caller's, and with ?compartmentId=<tenancy OCID> that tenancy's (a compartment OCID resolves to the caller's namespace).
  • A namespace in the path that is not the caller's is answered with 404 NamespaceNotFound, as on real OCI. Ask GetNamespace for the namespace instead of hard-coding one.
  • Pre-authenticated request URLs work for every tenancy: the token is looked up across tenancies in the request's region, must match the namespace in the URL, and acts as the tenancy that created it.
  • CopyObject honours destinationRegion (required, as on real OCI): the destination bucket must exist in that region and the copy lands there. The copy completes immediately; its work request (COMPLETED) is read from the source region.
  • Content-MD5 is verified on upload; opc-content-md5 is returned.
  • Object versioning, retention rules, lifecycle policies, replication and the Amazon S3 Compatibility API are not implemented yet.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: OCI Organizations (the Tenant Manager control plane), API version 20230401. A parent tenancy creates child tenancies; together they form an organization, and each child is linked to the parent per feature. Real OCI serves it on organizations.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Child tenancies CreateChildTenancy Organizations ListOrganizations, GetOrganization, UpdateOrganization Organization tenancies ListOrganizationTenancies, GetOrganizationTenancy Links ListLinks, GetLink, GetLinkWithTenancyNames Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (/20230401/workRequests)

docs.title: How isolation works
docs.text:
A child tenancy is a new tenancy OCID with its own home region. Requests signed with the child tenancy (its OCID as the first part of the Signature keyId) land in that tenancy's own, empty storage: they see none of the parent's resources, and GetTenancy reports the child's name and home region. This mirrors how floci-aws member accounts work.

A child homed in another region reaches that region by default: a request whose Host names no region (localhost:4599) lands in the signing tenancy's home region. Like any tenancy, the child can use other regions only after subscribing to them.

Organizations, organization tenancies and links are stored with the parent tenancy, so a child lists the same organization as its parent. Only the parent can update it or create more children: CreateChildTenancy signed by a child is 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateChildTenancy and UpdateOrganization return 202 with an opc-work-request-id header and no body. The work request is already SUCCEEDED; its resources[0].identifier is the new child tenancy OCID.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paged with opc-next-page.
  • GetOrganization, GetOrganizationTenancy and GetLink return an etag; UpdateOrganization honours if-match.
  • homeRegion must be a region the parent tenancy is subscribed to (its home region, or one added with CreateRegionSubscription); otherwise the request fails with 400 InvalidParameter.
  • compartmentId on CreateChildTenancy and ListOrganizations must be the caller's own tenancy; another tenancy is 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.
  • A CORE link is always created, plus one link per entry in features.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
The OCI SDKs leave these open, so floci-oci picks:

  • Organizations data is global. Real OCI serves this API on a regional host and does not say whether its data is shared across regions; floci-oci keeps organizations, organization tenancies, links and their work requests tenancy-wide, like Identity, so every region of the tenancy sees the same organization.
  • homeRegion accepts a region name (us-phoenix-1) or a region key (PHX).
  • governanceStatus defaults to OPTED_IN when omitted.
  • Organizations and links get global OCIDs: ocid1.organization.<realm>..… and ocid1.link.<realm>..…. A child tenancy's OCID uses the realm of its home region.
  • When no subscriptionId is given, the organization gets a synthetic ocid1.organizationssubscription… default subscription.

docs.title: Not implemented yet
docs.text: DeleteOrganizationTenancy, RestoreOrganizationTenancy, ApproveForTransfer, UnapproveForTransfer, DeleteLink, link features, invitations, governance (including governance rules), domains, subscriptions and orders. The child tenancy limit is not enforced, and no administrator user or policy is created in the child.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci organizations child-tenancy create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --tenancy-name dev --home-region us-ashburn-1 --admin-email admin@example.com
oci organizations organization list $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY"
oci organizations link list $E

docs.title: Database with PostgreSQL
docs.text: OCI Database with PostgreSQL, API version 20220915 (SDK package psql, client PostgresqlClient, CLI oci psql). Each DB system is backed by a real PostgreSQL container, so the endpoint and certificate returned by GetConnectionDetails are ones an application can connect to. Real OCI serves the API on postgresql.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations DB systems CreateDbSystem, GetDbSystem, ListDbSystems, UpdateDbSystem, DeleteDbSystem, ChangeDbSystemCompartment Runtime StartDbSystem, StopDbSystem, RestartDbInstanceInDbSystem, ResetMasterUserPassword Connection GetConnectionDetails, GetPrimaryDbInstance, UpdateDbSystemDbInstance Catalog ListShapes, ListDefaultConfigurations, GetDefaultConfiguration Work requests GetWorkRequest, ListWorkRequests, ListWorkRequestErrors, ListWorkRequestLogs

docs.title: How a DB system runs
docs.text:
• One container per DB system. CreateDbSystem returns the system CREATING with an IN_PROGRESS work request and starts a postgres:<major>-alpine container in the background. Once PostgreSQL accepts connections the system becomes ACTIVE and the work request SUCCEEDED, which is what Terraform and oci psql db-system create --wait-for-state wait on. A container that exits, or one that is not ready within FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 120), marks both FAILED, and the reason is listed by ListWorkRequestErrors.
  • Version and image. dbVersion takes a major (15) or a major and minor (15.8); its major picks the image through FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_IMAGE (default postgres:{major}-alpine). Once the server is up, dbVersion reports the server's own version, such as 15.8.
  • Endpoint. PostgreSQL's port is published on a host port from FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_BASE_PORT..MAX_PORT (default 15432..15531), one per DB system. GetConnectionDetails returns localhost and that port when floci-oci runs on the host. When floci-oci runs in a container it returns the PostgreSQL container's name and port 5432, for clients on the same Docker network; set FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_ENDPOINT_MODE=published to get the Docker host and the published port instead, for clients on the host.
  • TLS. Every DB system has its own self-signed certificate, returned as caCertificate. PostgreSQL serves it, so sslmode=verify-full works with that file as sslrootcert. Unencrypted connections are accepted too.
  • Credentials. The admin user and password come from credentials (PLAIN_TEXT, or VAULT_SECRET read from a secret in floci-oci's own Vault). As on real OCI the password is never returned, and floci-oci does not store it either. ResetMasterUserPassword changes it in the running database.
  • Stop, start, restart. StopDbSystem removes the container and keeps the data volume (INACTIVE); StartDbSystem and RestartDbInstanceInDbSystem bring it back with the same data, and the same host port when it is still free.
  • Delete. DeleteDbSystem removes the container. The DB system stays readable as DELETED, as on real OCI, since clients poll it to see the delete finish. The data volume is removed in memory storage mode or when prune-volumes-on-delete is set, like the other sidecars.
  • Mock mode. FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_MOCK=true starts no container: every DB system is ACTIVE at once and every operation completes immediately, with nothing listening on the endpoint. Useful where Docker is not available.
  • Teardown. Containers are stopped on shutdown and removed, with their volumes, by POST /_floci-oci/state/reset, whatever prune-volumes-on-delete says. After a restart of floci-oci with persistent storage, the DB systems that were ACTIVE are started again. An operation the restart interrupted is settled first: a delete finishes, a create ends FAILED (its master password was never stored), and a stop, restart or password reset fails its work request, leaving the system ACTIVE as it was.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateDbSystem returns 200 with the DB system, an etag and opc-work-request-id. Every other mutation returns 202 with opc-work-request-id and no body.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paged with opc-next-page.
  • shape accepts what Terraform sends (PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB, or PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex with instanceOcpuCount and instanceMemorySizeInGBs) and the bare shape. The response carries the bare shape and both sizes.
  • storageDetails.availabilityDomain is required when isRegionallyDurable is false and rejected when it is true (400 InvalidParameter).
  • Operations need the right state: StartDbSystem an INACTIVE system, the others an ACTIVE one. Otherwise they return 409 IncorrectState.
  • compartmentId must be an existing compartment or the tenancy, and the request must be sent to a region the tenancy is subscribed to, like every other regional service.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
OCI's SDKs leave these open, so floci-oci picks:

  • Versions and shapes. Majors 14 and 15 and shapes VM.Standard.E4.Flex and VM.Standard.E5.Flex are the ones Oracle's Terraform examples use. 16 and 17 are accepted as well so newer versions can be tried. Anything else is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • OCIDs. ocid1.postgresqldbsystem…, ocid1.postgresqldbinstance… and ocid1.postgresqldefaultconfiguration…. A default configuration OCID is the same on every start.
  • Default configurations. Each version has a flexible one and a fixed one per shape and size. A DB system created with a sized shape (PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB) gets the fixed configuration for that size, and one created with a bare shape and separate sizes gets the flexible one, which is what Terraform needs to show no changes on the next plan.
  • Work requests. The resource entity type is postgresqlDbSystem. Start, stop, restart and password reset report UPDATE_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM, since the API has no value of their own.
  • credentials is required on create, because only a fresh DB system can be created.
  • Several instances are one database. instanceCount above 1 gives that many instance records, all served by the one container; there are no replicas.
  • Defaults. When omitted: 2 OCPUs and 32 GB, 75000 IOPS, maintenance window SUN 00:00, backup policy NONE, and the default configuration for the version.
  • Network. subnetId and nsgIds are stored unchecked, since there is no networking service.
  • Update is metadata only. Shape, sizes, IOPS and management policy change what the API reports, not the running container.

docs.title: Not implemented yet
docs.text: Backups, restore and point-in-time recovery; custom configurations (configId must be a default configuration); replicas, failover, switchover, role changes and PatchDbSystem; Kerberos and insights; creating a DB system from a backup or another DB system (501). The DB system service limit is not enforced.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

# Create a DB system and wait for it
ID=$(oci psql db-system create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name demo-db \
  --db-version 16 --shape PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB \
  --network-details '{"subnetId":"ocid1.subnet.oc1.iad.demo"}' \
  --storage-details '{"systemType":"OCI_OPTIMIZED_STORAGE","isRegionallyDurable":true}' \
  --credentials '{"username":"admin_user","passwordDetails":{"passwordType":"PLAIN_TEXT","password":"BEstrO0ng_#11"}}' \
  --wait-for-state SUCCEEDED --query 'data.resources[0].identifier' --raw-output)

# Where to connect, and the certificate to trust
oci psql connection-details get $E --db-system-id "$ID" > connection.json
jq -r '.data."ca-certificate"' connection.json > ca.pem
PORT=$(jq -r '.data."primary-db-endpoint".port' connection.json)

psql "host=localhost port=$PORT dbname=postgres user=admin_user sslmode=verify-full sslrootcert=ca.pem"

docs.title: Queue
docs.text: OCI Queue — API version 20210201. Control plane and data plane are both served on port 4599; the queue's messagesEndpoint points back at the emulator.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Queues CreateQueue, GetQueue, ListQueues, UpdateQueue, DeleteQueue, ChangeCompartment, PurgeQueue Messages PutMessages, GetMessages, DeleteMessage(s), UpdateMessage(s) Observability GetStats, ListChannels Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (/20210201/workRequests)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every control-plane mutation is work-request driven: 202 with an opc-work-request-id header and no body. Poll GetWorkRequest — the emulator records the queue OCID in resources[] and sets timeFinished immediately, which is what Terraform's retry predicate requires.
  • Lists are wrapped — {"items":[…]} — unlike Identity's bare arrays.
  • sortBy values are camelCase (timeCreated, displayName), not the SCREAMING_CASE KMS uses.
  • retentionInSeconds is set at create time and is not updatable.

docs.title: Message semantics
docs.text:
• visibilityInSeconds defaults to the queue's setting; 0 is a peek — the message stays visible but its deliveryCount still increments.
  • timeoutInSeconds > 0 long-polls until a message arrives (capped at 10s in the emulator); 0 short-polls.
  • With deadLetterQueueDeliveryCount > 0, over-delivered messages move to the DLQ and show up under dlq in GetStats.
  • Messages expire after retentionInSeconds.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci queue queue create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name demo
oci queue messages put-messages $E --queue-id <queueId> \
  --messages '[{"content":"hello queue"}]'
oci queue messages get-messages $E --queue-id <queueId>

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Consumer groups, channel consumption limits and per-channel purge filters beyond channelIds are not implemented.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text: OCI Streaming — API version 20180418. Kafka-like partitioned append-only logs with cursor-based consumption.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Streams CreateStream, GetStream, ListStreams, UpdateStream, DeleteStream Produce PutMessages Consume CreateCursor, CreateGroupCursor, GetMessages Groups ConsumerCommit, ConsumerHeartbeat, GetGroup, UpdateGroup Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (/20180418/workRequests)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateStream is dual-mode: it returns the full Stream body and an opc-work-request-id header. Terraform waits on the work request and reads the stream OCID from its resources[] (entityType containing stream, actionType CREATED).
  • Lists are bare JSON arrays. retentionInHours is on Stream but not on StreamSummary, so it only appears on Get.
  • GetMessages takes a mandatory cursor query parameter, returns a bare array and advances through the opc-next-cursor response header.
  • Message key and value are base64; Message.stream carries the stream name, not its OCID.
  • Commit and heartbeat are POSTs with the cursor in the query string and an empty body.

docs.title: Partitioning and cursors
docs.text:
• Messages with a key hash to a stable partition; keyless messages round-robin.
  • Cursor types: TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, AT_OFFSET, AFTER_OFFSET, AT_TIME. Group cursors support only TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, AT_TIME.
  • Cursors are opaque (base64) and bound to their stream — using one against another stream is a 400.
  • Committing a group cursor persists per-partition offsets; a fresh group cursor for the same group resumes from them.

TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci streaming admin stream create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --name demo-stream --partitions 2

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Stream pools are synthesized (a pool OCID is minted per stream) and their Kafka connection settings, connect harnesses and the archiver are not implemented.
